## DynamoDB backend implementation for Teleport.

### Introduction

This package enables Teleport auth server to store secrets in 
[DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/) on AWS.

WARNING: Using DynamoDB involves recurring charge from AWS.

The table created by the backend will provision 5/5 R/W capacity.
It should be covered by the free tier.

### Running tests

The DynamodDB tests are not run by default. To run them locally, try:

```
go test -tags dynamodb -v  ./lib/backend/dynamo
```

*NOTE:* you will need to provide a AWS credentials & a default region 
(e.g. in your `~/.aws/credentials` & `~/.aws/config` files, or via
environment vars) for the tests to work.

### Quick Start

Add this storage configuration in `teleport` section of the config file (by default it's `/etc/teleport.yaml`):

```yaml
teleport:
  storage:
    type: dynamodb
    region: eu-west-1
    table_name: teleport.state
    access_key: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
    secret_key: YYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY
```

Replace `region` and `table_name` with your own settings. Teleport will create the table automatically.

### AWS IAM Role

You can use IAM role instead of hard coded access and secret key (IAM role is
recommended).  You must apply correct policy in order to the auth to
create/get/update K/V in DynamoDB.

Example of a typical policy (change region and account ID):

```json
{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Sid": "AllAPIActionsOnTeleportAuth",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": "dynamodb:*",
            "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-west-1:123456789012:table/prod.teleport.auth"
        }
    ]
}
```

item.text: The backend currently creates every table with provisioned throughput and enables scaling from configuration without checking the table’s actual billing mode. I’ll make creation mode explicit, use the reported mode for existing tables, and cover both paths with local tests.

The code now defaults new tables to on-demand, validates `billing_mode`, and skips scaling for an existing table that reports on-demand billing. I also updated the existing autoscaling integration test to request provisioned mode explicitly. I’m running the package tests now.

item.text:
Implemented DynamoDB `billing_mode`. New tables default to `pay_per_request`, which omits provisioned throughput and ignores capacity unit settings and auto scaling. `provisioned` uses the configured capacity units and permits auto scaling. Initialization now checks an existing table’s billing mode and logs when it ignores auto scaling for an on-demand table.

Updated the [backend documentation](/app/lib/backend/dynamo/README.md) and added [billing mode tests](/app/lib/backend/dynamo/billing_mode_test.go). The package tests and focused DynamoDB tagged tests pass. The AWS integration tests were not run.
